chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saying: When a man divorces his wife and she claims to be pregnant, he should wait for nine months. If she gives birth, [the waiting period is complete]; otherwise, she observes a waiting period of three months, and then she is irrevocably divorced from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a divorced woman who claims to be pregnant according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the default presumption of pregnancy in cases of disputed paternity, requiring the husband to wait nine months for confirmation. If birth occurs, the iddah ends immediately; otherwise, the woman completes a three-month iddah before the divorce is finalized, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of balancing certainty with the benefit of the doubt. This ruling underscores the importance of the waiting period (iddah) in determining lineage and marital status in Islamic family law.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I heard Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>) saying: ‘When the man divorces his wife, so she waits while pregnant, she should wait for nine months. So if she were to give birth, or else she should wait three months, then she is irrevocably divorced from him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from af-Fadf ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj who has said the following: “

I once heard abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’If one divorces his wife and she claims to be pregnant, he must wait for nine months if she gives birth, otherwise, she counts a waiting period of three months.’”
